title: Open-Source Pipeline with Tesseract OCR and spaCy
description:
A self-hosted pipeline built only from open-source parts, for teams that cannot send documents to a cloud service.

  • Text: the PDF text layer is read with pypdf; scans and images go through Tesseract OCR after cleanup with Pillow (grayscale, contrast, denoise, binarize).
  • Document type: a TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier (scikit-learn) labels invoices, contracts, receipts and reports.
  • Fields: spaCy with an EntityRuler finds dates, amounts and e-mail addresses without downloading a model; rules turn them into invoice number, dates, subtotal, tax, total or contract parties and dates.
  • Checks: required fields, subtotal + tax = total and date order decide between valid, requires_review and invalid.
  • A FastAPI service with a Dockerfile (including Tesseract) exposes it as POST /documents.
implementationSteps: Install Tesseract (the Dockerfile adds tesseract-ocr) and the pinned Python packages.
Read the text layer of PDFs with pypdf; if a page has almost no text, OCR its embedded images.
Clean up images (grayscale, autocontrast, median filter, threshold) and run Tesseract with --oem 3 --psm 6.
Classify the document type with TF-IDF + logistic regression; retrain it on your own labelled documents.
Run a blank spaCy English pipeline with EntityRuler patterns for dates, money and e-mail addresses.
Map entities to fields from the words before them on the same line (Total, VAT, Due, effective, between ... and ...).
Normalize dates to ISO and amounts to numbers, then validate required fields, totals and date order.
Serve the pipeline with FastAPI: file type and size limits, random temp file names, clear error codes.
Measure field accuracy on a labelled sample of your documents and add rules or a trained NER model where it falls short.
performance:
Targets, not measured results:

  • Header fields (number, dates, totals) correct on at least 95 % of clean, labelled invoices in your own sample.
  • Text PDFs take well under a second; OCR typically takes a few seconds per page on one CPU core, depending on resolution.
  • Throughput scales with the number of worker processes; no per-page fees.
userExperience: Teams send a file to one REST endpoint and get JSON back: document type with confidence, extracted fields, how the text was obtained (text layer or OCR) and a validation status with reasons. Documents never leave your own servers, and rules can be adjusted in code when a new layout shows up.
